STATE OF EMERGENCY FOR WINTER WEATHER

The National Weather Service predicts that an Arctic blast will
impact Georgia with frigid temperatures, beginning on December 22,
2022; and

Projected precipitation on the evening of December 22, 2022
through the morning of December 23, 2022, followed by severe cold
temperatures projected across the State beginning December 23,
2022 and continuing through December 26, 2022, creates the
potential for black ice formation; and

Wind gusts of more than 20 miles per hour are projected to
accompany the cold front and may exacerbate potential property
damage, including downed trees and powerlines; and

Due to the possibility of black ice accumulating on roadways and low
temperatures, this projected winter weather poses a danger to the
people of Georgia; and

Due to the low temperatures, the efficient transportation and supply
of heating fuel is essential to maintain public safety; and

Assistance from the State of Georgia is necessary to provide for the
public's safety and mitigate potential consequences of this winter
weather; and

The Federal Motor Carrier Safety regulations, 49 C.F.R. § 390, et
seq., limit the hours that operators of commercial motor vehicles
may drive; and

49 C.F.R. § 390.23 allows the Governor of a State to suspend these
rules and regulations for up to 30 days if the Governor determines
that an emergency condition exists; and

On April 14, 2022, due to the ongoing severe disruptions to Georgia’s
supply chain, I issued Executive Order 04.14.22.01, declaring a State
of Emergency for Supply Chain Disruptions; and

On May 10, 2022, I renewed the State of Emergency for Supply Chain
Disruptions until June 14, 2022, by issuing Executive Order
05.10.22.01; and

On May 26, 2022, I renewed the State of Emergency for Supply Chain
Disruptions until July 14, 2022, by issuing Executive Order
05.26.22.01; and

On July 1, 2022, I renewed the State of Emergency for Supply Chain
Disruptions until August 13, 2022, by issuing Executive Order
07.01.22.01; and

On August 3, 2022, I renewed the State of Emergency for Supply
Chain Disruptions until September 12, 2022, by issuing Executive
Order 08.03.22.01; and

On September 1, 2022, I renewed the State of Emergency for Supply
Chain Disruptions until October 12, 2022, by issuing Executive
Order 09.01.22.01; and

On October 3, 2022, I renewed the State of Emergency for Supply
Chain Disruptions until November 11, 2022, by issuing Executive
Order 10.03.22.01; and

On November 4, 2022, I renewed the State of Emergency for Supply
Chain Disruptions until December 11, 2022, by issuing Executive
Order 11.04.22.01; and

On December 8, 2022, I renewed the State of Emergency for Supply
Chain Disruptions until January 10, 2023, by issuing Executive
Order 12.08.22.01; and

This Order shall create a coexisting state of emergency in the State of
Georgia with the State of Emergency for Supply Chain Disruptions
described in the immediately preceding paragraphs; and

The responses by the State to this State of Emergency for Winter
Weather and the State of Emergency for Supply Chain Disruptions
should both proceed simultaneously, without one impeding the
other; and

The Governor is vested with the emergency powers cited herein as
the Chief Executive of this State; and

ORDERED:

As Chief Executive, the Governor is tasked with protecting the
citizens of this State, including during a state of emergency; and

Code Section 38-3-51 vests the Governor with the authority to bring
emergency situations under control by issuing orders, rules, and
regulations to protect the safety and welfare of the public; and

Code Section 38-3-28 provides that "[a]ll orders, rules, and
regulations promulgated by the Governor" have the force and effect
of law; and

In consultation with state emergency preparedness officials, I have
determined that the following actions are necessary and appropriate
to protect the health, safety, and welfare of Georgia's residents and
visitors.

NOW, THEREFORE, PURSUANT TO CODE SECTION 38-3-51, AND
THE AUTHORITY VESTED IN ME AS GOVERNOR OF THE STATE OF
GEORGIA, IT IS HEREBY

That a State of Emergency exists in in the State of Georgia due to the
potential of severe winter weather affecting the State on December
22, 2022 through December 26, 2022.

IT IS FURTHER

That the State of Emergency declared by this Order shall coexist with
the State of Emergency for Supply Chain Disruptions declared by
Executive Order 04.14.22.01 and renewed by Executive Orders
05.10.22.01, 05.26.22.01, 07.01.22.01, 08.03.22.01, 09.01.22.01,
10.03.22.01, 11.04.22.01, and 12.08.22.01. The existence or
termination of one shall not impinge the other.

IT IS FURTHER

That any orders derivative of or appurtenant to this Order addressing
this State of Emergency for Winter Weather shall not infringe,
overturn, or in any way amend any orders that have been issued for
the purpose of responding to the State of Emergency for Supply
Chain Disruptions declared by Executive Order 04.14.22.01 and
renewed by Executive Orders 05.10.22.01, 05.26.22.01, 07.01.22.01,
08.03.22.01, 09.01.22.01, 10.03.22.01, 11.04.22.01, and 12.08.22.01.

IT IS FURTHER

That all resources of the state of Georgia be made available to assist
in preparation, response, and recovery activities throughout the

affected areas, and the Georgia Emergency Management and
Homeland Security Agency shall activate the Georgia Emergency
Operations Plan.

IT IS FURTHER

That state agencies shall coordinate all public and emergency
information, activities, releases, and response efforts related to this
emergency with the Georgia Emergency Management and
Homeland Security Agency.

IT IS FURTHER

That the Georgia Department of Transportation and Georgia
Department of Public Safety shall take all necessary action to ensure
the expeditious movement of utility vehicles, equipment, and
personnel through the State to eliminate power outages.

IT IS FURTHER

That state agencies shall provide sufficient personnel required for the
staffing of the Georgia State Operations Center or other command,
control, and coordination points as may be designated by the
Director of the Georgia Emergency Management and Homeland
Security Agency and shall provide such personnel, vehicles,
equipment, and other resources needed to protect life and property
and to ensure continuation, restoration, and recovery of essential
public services.

IT IS FURTHER

That the federal rules and regulations limiting hours that operators
of commercial vehicles may drive are suspended to ensure the
uninterrupted supply of goods and services necessary to respond to
this State of Emergency, including petroleum products, propane, and
heating fuels. This declared emergency justifies a suspension of Part
395 (driver's hours of service) of Title 49 of the Code of Federal
Regulations. The suspension will remain in effect for thirty (30) days
or until the emergency condition ceases to exist, whichever is less.
Nothing herein will be construed as an exemption from the
Commercial Driver's License requirements in 49 C.F.R. § 383 and
the financial requirements in 49 C.F.R. § 387.

IT IS FURTHER

That no motor carrier operating under the terms of this State of
Emergency for Winter Weather will require or allow an ill or fatigued

driver to operate a motor vehicle. A driver who notifies a motor
vehicle carrier that he or she needs immediate rest will be given at
least ten (10) consecutive hours off-duty before being required to
return to service.

IT IS FURTHER

Pursuant to Code Section 10-1-393.4, price gouging related to goods
and services necessary to respond to this State of Emergency,
including petroleum products, propane, and heating fuels, would be
detrimental to the social and economic welfare of the citizens of this
State and is therefore prohibited.

IT IS FURTHER

That if one or more of the provisions contained in this Order shall be
held to be invalid, in violation of the Georgia Constitution, in
violation of Georgia law, or unenforceable in any respect, such
invalidity, violation, or unenforceability shall not affect any other
provisions of this Order, but, in such case, this Order shall be
construed as if such invalid, illegal, or unenforceable provision had
never been contained within the Order.

IT IS FURTHER

That no provision of this Order shall limit, infringe, suspend, or
supplant any judicial order, judgment, or decree issued pursuant to
the laws or constitution of this State or the laws or constitution of the
United States, nor shall any person use any provision this Order as a
defense to an action in violation of a judicial order, judgment, or
decree by any court created pursuant to the laws or constitution of
this State or the laws or constitution of the United States.

IT IS FURTHER
The Office of the Governor may continue to issue guidance on the
scope of this Order as needed through communication media,

including social media, without need for further Executive Orders.

IT IS FURTHER

All provisions of the Order shall become effective upon signature and
shall be valid for a period of six (6) days, expiring December 26,
2022, at 11:59 P.M. unless this State of Emergency is renewed by the
Governor.

There currently exist at the University of Georgia Attapulgus Research and Education
Center, Decatur County, Attapulgus, Georgia, two residential buildings (#4850 and
#4851) and one storage barn (#4860) (collectively, the “Buildings”), located at 254 N.
Griffin Avenue; and

The Board of Regents’ Policy 9.8.2.3 DEMOLITION authorizes the Chancellor or Vice
Chancellor for Facilities to declare buildings, structures and other improvements no
longer advantageously useful to the University System of Georgia. Said Buildings are
included within this policy; and

It has been determined by Ms. Sandra Lynn Neuse, Vice Chancellor for Facilities of the
Board of Regents of the University System of Georgia, that said Buildings can no longer be
advantageously used by the University of Georgia or the University System of Georgia and
should be removed.

Now, THEREFORE, BY THE POWER VESTED IN ME AS GOVERNOR OF THE STATE OF
GEORGIA, IT IS HEREBY

That the Board of Regents of the University System of Georgia is hereby authorized to
demolish and remove the Buildings from the University of Georgia Attapulgus Research
and Education Center, Decatur County, Attapulgus, Georgia.

IT IS FURTHER
That the appropriate staff of the University of Georgia, acting under the approval of the
Board of Regents of the University System of Georgia, is hereby authorized to demolish

Georgia, passed away on Saturday, December 17, 2022; and

Judge Reese honorably served the citizens of Georgia first as an Assistant Attorney
General in the Georgia Department of Law, and later as counsel for the Georgia
Department of Insurance, the Subsequent Injury Trust Fund, and the State Health
Planning Agency; and

Judge Reese also served as Commissioner of the Department of Community Health
and the Department of Human Services before his 2016 appointment to the Court
of Appeals of the State of Georgia; and

It is fitting and proper to recognize Judge Reese’s service to citizens of the State of
Georgia by lowering the flags throughout Georgia to half-staff.

NOW, THEREFORE, IN HONOR OF AND AS A MARK OF RESPECT FOR THE MEMORY
OF THE HONORABLE CLYDE L. REESE, PURSUANT TO THE AUTHORITY VESTED IN
ME AS GOVERNOR OF THE STATE OF GEORGIA, IT IS HEREBY

That the flag of the United States and the flag of the State of Georgia be flown at
half-staff on all State buildings and grounds on Monday, December 19, 2022, and

until sunset on the day of Judge Reese’s interment.

FOR SUPPLY CHAIN DISRUPTIONS

On April 14, 2022, due to the ongoing severe disruptions to Georgia’s
supply chain, I issued Executive Order 04.14.22.01, declaring a State of
Emergency for Supply Chain Disruptions; and

On May 10, 2022, I renewed the State of Emergency for Supply Chain
Disruptions until June 14, 2022, by issuing Executive Order 05.10.22.01;
and

On May 26, 2022, I renewed the State of Emergency for Supply Chain
Disruptions until July 14, 2022, by issuing Executive Order 05.26.22.01;
and

On July 1, 2022, I renewed the State of Emergency for Supply Chain
Disruptions until August 13, 2022, by issuing Executive Order 07.01.22.01;
and

On August 3, 2022, I renewed the State of Emergency for Supply Chain
Disruptions until September 12, 2022, by issuing Executive Order
08.03.22.01; and

On September 1, 2022, I renewed the State of Emergency for Supply Chain
Disruptions until October 12, 2022, by issuing Executive Order
09.01.22.01; and

On October 3, 2022, I renewed the State of Emergency for Supply Chain
Disruptions until November 11, 2022, by issuing Executive Order
10.03.22.01; and

On November 4, 2022, I renewed the State of Emergency for Supply Chain
Disruptions until December 11, 2022, by issuing Executive Order
11.04.22.01; and

On December 8, 2022, I renewed the State of Emergency for Supply Chain
Disruptions until January 10, 2023, by issuing Executive Order
12.08.22.01; and

On November 4, 2022, I issued Executive Order 11.04.22.02 extending the
suspensions of the collection of motor fuel and diesel fuel taxes required by
Code Section 48-9-3 and the collection of sales taxes on locomotive fuel
required by Code Section 48-8-30 through December 11, 2022; and

The supply chain disruptions affecting the cost of fuel have not been fully
alleviated since I issued Executive Orders 05.26.22.02, 07.01.22.02,
08.03.22.02, 09.01.22.02, 10.03.22.02, and 11.04.22.02, and the high cost
of fuel continues to negatively impact Georgia’s residents and economy;
and

The Governor is vested with the emergency powers cited herein as the Chief
Executive of this State; and

Code Section 38-3-28 provides that “[a]ll orders, rules, and regulations
promulgated by the Governor” have the force and effect of law; and

As Chief Executive, the Governor is tasked with protecting the citizens of
this State, including during a state of emergency; and

Code Section 38-3-51(c)(1) vests the Governor with the power to enforce all
laws, rules, and regulations relating to emergency management and to
assume direct operational control of all civil forces and helpers in the state;

Code Section 38-3-51(c)(4) vests the Governor with the power to perform
and exercise such other functions, powers, and duties as may be deemed
necessary to promote and secure the safety and protection of the civilian
population; and

Code Section 38-3-51(d)(1) vests the Governor with the power to suspend
any regulatory statute prescribing the procedures for conduct of state
business, or the orders, rules, or regulations of any state agency if strict
compliance with any statute, order, rule, or regulation would in any way
prevent, hinder, or delay necessary action in coping with the emergency or
disaster; and

Code Section 45-12-22 vests the Governor with the power to suspend the
collection of taxes, or any part thereof, due the state until the next meeting
of the General Assembly but no longer; and

In the event the Governor has declared a state of emergency, Code Section
45-12-22 vests him with the power to suspend the collection of state motor
fuel taxes, subject to ratification by the General Assembly at its next
meeting; and

In consultation with state economic, transportation, and emergency
preparedness officials, I have determined that the following actions are
necessary and appropriate to protect the continued strength of Georgia’s
economy and provide for the health, safety, and welfare of Georgia’s
residents and visitors.

NOW, THEREFORE, PURSUANT TO CODE SECTION 38-3-51, AND THE
AUTHORITY VESTED IN ME AS GOVERNOR OF THE STATE OF GEORGIA,
IT IS HEREBY

That pursuant to Code Section 45-12-22, the collection of motor fuel and
diesel fuel taxes required by Code Section 48-9-3 is hereby suspended for
the effective dates of this Order.

IT IS FURTHER

That no distributor of motor fuel or diesel fuel shall be found in violation
of Code Section 48-9-17 for complying with the terms of this Order.

IT IS FURTHER

That the collection of tax required by Code Section 48-8-30 upon the retail
purchase, retail sale, rental, storage, use, or consumption of fuel to a
contract or common carrier regulated by the United States Surface
Transportation Board for use exclusively in the operation of locomotives by

Mr. Vincent Joseph Dooley, the iconic former University of Georgia football
coach and athletic director, passed away on Friday, October 28, 2022; and

Achievement Award, cementing his place among the all-time coaching
greats and recognizing his excellence in coaching on and off the field; and

athletic programs achieved 23 national championships, 78 conference
championships, and had numerous finishes in the top 10 for best overall
athletic departments in the nation, including a second-place finish in 1998-
1999; and

Coach Dooley’s dedication to public service extended far beyond the football
field and the University of Georgia, as he served as the state chairman for
the Georgia Easter Seals Society for over 30 years, including being named
National Volunteer of the Year in 1987, and contributed selfless charitable
work for organizations such as The Heart Fund and Boy Scouts of America,
and issues including multiple sclerosis, juvenile diabetes, and
homelessness; and

WHEREAS:

STATE OF EMERGENCY FOR SEVERE FLOODING

On September 4, 2022, heavy rainfall accumulated in parts of
Northwest Georgia resulting in widespread flooding in Chattooga
and Floyd Counties; and

The National Weather Service issued a Particularly Dangerous
Situation (“PDS”) advisory during the early morning hours of
Sunday, September 4, 2022, that was subsequently elevated to a
Flash Flood Warning; and

Due to the estimated twelve (12) inches of rain, this severe weather
event has caused and will likely continue to cause rivers to rise
rapidly causing significant localized downstream flooding; and

Preliminary assessments from county emergency management
agencies and the Georgia Emergency Management and Homeland
Security Agency indicate a need for assistance in the impacted
counties; and

Assistance from the State of Georgia is necessary to provide for the
public's safety, protect public and private property, and restore the
social and economic welfare of Chattooga and Floyd Counties; and

On April 14, 2022, due to the ongoing severe disruptions to Georgia’s
supply chain, I issued Executive Order 04.14.22.01, declaring a State
of Emergency for Supply Chain Disruptions; and

On May 10, 2022, I renewed the State of Emergency for Supply Chain
Disruptions until June 14, 2022, by issuing Executive Order
05.10.22.01; and

ORDERED:

On August 11, 2022, I appointed a committee consisting of Attorney
General Christopher Carr, Sheriff Rod Howell of Colquitt County,
and Sheriff Ashley Paulk of Lowndes County to investigate Sheriff
Richard Morgan of Miller County after he was arrested by the
Georgia Bureau of Investigation and charged with one count of
Sexual Battery and one count of Violation of Oath by Public Officer,
by issuing Executive Order 08.11.22.03; and

On August 26, 2022, the committee delivered its recommendation to
me that, based on the committee’s investigation and findings, Sheriff
Morgan be suspended pursuant to Code Section 15-16-26(c).

NOW, THEREFORE, PURSUANT TO CODE SECTION 15-16-26 AND
THE AUTHORITY VESTED IN ME AS GOVERNOR OF THE STATE OF
GEORGIA, IT IS HEREBY

That Sheriff Morgan is hereby suspended from the Office of Sheriff
of Miller County for a period of sixty (60) days, effective immediately.

IT IS FURTHER

That pursuant to Code Section 15-16-26(d), the Chief Judge of the
Pataula Judicial Circuit shall appoint a person who meets the
qualifications for sheriffs pursuant to Code Section 15-16-1 to assume
the duties and responsibilities of the Office of Sheriff of Miller County
during the period of Sheriff Morgan’s suspension.

Mrs. Sandra Dunagan Deal, former First Lady of Georgia, passed away on Tuesday,
August 23, 2022; and

As First Lady of Georgia from 2011 to 2019, and alongside Georgia’s 82 Governor
Nathan Deal, she promoted community service, education, and literacy initiatives;
and

During her time as First Lady, and as a passionate advocate for literacy and student
achievement, she read to students in all of Georgia’s 159 counties and 181 school
districts, including 800 schools and Pre-K programs; and

For generations to come, the Sandra Dunagan Deal Center for Early Language and
Literacy, located on the campus of her alma mater, Georgia College & State
University, will continue her good work in bringing the gift of reading to Georgia’s
children; and

During her time in the Governor’s Mansion, while improving its beauty and
preserving its memories for futures generations, Mrs. Deal co-authored a book,
“Memories of the Mansion,” which covered the rich history of the Governor's
Mansion and experiences of Georgia’s first families; and

It is fitting and proper to recognize Mrs. Sandra Deal’s life and service to citizens of
the State of Georgia by lowering the flags throughout Georgia to half-staff.

NOW, THEREFORE, IN HONOR OF AND AS A MARK OF RESPECT FOR THE MEMORY
OF MRS. SANDRA DUNAGAN DEAL, PURSUANT TO THE AUTHORITY VESTED IN
ME AS GOVERNOR OF THE STATE OF GEORGIA, IT IS HEREBY

That the flag of the United States and the flag of the State of Georgia be flown at
half-staff on all State buildings and grounds on Saturday, August 27, 2022, the day

of Mrs. Deal’s interment.

SUSPENDING FUEL TAXES DURING THE STATE OF EMERGENCY

WHEREAS:

WHEREAS:

WHEREAS:

WHEREAS:

WHEREAS:

WHEREAS:

FOR SUPPLY CHAIN DISRUPTIONS

On April 14, 2022, due to the ongoing severe disruptions to Georgia's
supply chain, I issued Executive Order 04.14.22.01, declaring a State of
Emergency for Supply Chain Disruptions; and

On May 10, 2022, I renewed the State of Emergency for Supply Chain
Disruptions until June 14, 2022, by issuing Executive Order 05.10.22.01;
and

On May 26, 2022, I renewed the State of Emergency for Supply Chain
Disruptions until July 14, 2022, by issuing Executive Order 05.26.22.01;
and

On July 1, 2022, I renewed the State of Emergency for Supply Chain
Disruptions until August 13, 2022, by issuing Executive Order 07.01.22.01;
and

On August 3, 2022, I renewed the State of Emergency for Supply Chain
Disruptions until September 12, 2022, by issuing Executive Order
08.03.22.01; and

On May 26, 2022, I issued Executive Order 05.26.22.02 suspending the
collection of motor fuel and diesel fuel taxes required by Code Section 48-
9-3 through July 14, 2022; and

On July 1, 2022, I issued Executive Order 07.01.22.02 extending the
suspension of the collection of motor fuel and diesel fuel taxes required by
Code Section 48-9-3 and suspending the collection of sales taxes on
locomotive fuel required by Code Section 48-8-30 through August 13,
2022; and

The supply chain disruptions affecting the cost of fuel have not been fully
alleviated since I issued Executive Orders 05.26.22.01 and 07.01.22.02,
and the high cost of fuel continues to negatively impact Georgia’s residents
and economy; and

WHEREAS:

WHEREAS:

WHEREAS:

WHEREAS:

WHEREAS:

WHEREAS:

WHEREAS:

WHEREAS:

WHEREAS:

ORDERED:

The Governor is vested with the emergency powers cited herein as the Chief
Executive of this State; and

Code Section 38-3-28 provides that “[a]ll orders, rules, and regulations
promulgated by the Governor” have the force and effect of law; and

As Chief Executive, the Governor is tasked with protecting the citizens of
this State, including during a state of emergency; and.

Code Section 38-3-51(c)(4) vests the Governor with the power to enforce all
laws, rules, and regulations relating to emergency management and to
assume direct operational control of all civil forces and helpers in the state;
and

Code Section 38-3-51(c)(4) vests the Governor with the power to perform
and exercise such other functions, powers, and duties as may be deemed
necessary to promote and secure the safety and protection of the civilian
population; and

Code Section 38-3-51(d)(1) vests the Governor with the power to suspend
any regulatory statute prescribing the procedures for conduct of state
business, or the orders, rules, or regulations of any state agency if strict
compliance with any statute, order, rule, or regulation would in any way
prevent, hinder, or delay necessary action in coping with the emergency or
disaster; and

Code Section 45-12-22 vests the Governor with the power to suspend the
collection of taxes, or any part thereof, due the state until the next meeting
of the General Assembly but no longer; and

In the event the Governor has declared a state of emergency, Code Section
45-12-22 vests him with the power to suspend the collection of state motor
fuel taxes, subject to ratification by the General Assembly at its next
meeting; and

In consultation with state economic, transportation, and emergency
preparedness officials, I have determined that the following actions are
necessary and appropriate to protect the continued strength of Georgia’s
economy and provide for the health, safety, and welfare of Georgia’s
residents and visitors.

NOW, THEREFORE, PURSUANT TO CODE SECTION 38-3-51, AND THE
AUTHORITY VESTED IN ME AS GOVERNOR OF THE STATE OF GEORGIA,
IT IS HEREBY

That pursuant to Code Section 45-12-22, the collection of motor fuel and
diesel fuel taxes required by Code Section 48-9-3 is hereby suspended for
the effective dates of this Order.

Page 20f3

IT IS FURTHER

ORDERED: That no distributor of motor fuel or diesel fuel shall be found in violation
of Code Section 48-9-17 for complying with the terms of this Order.

Ir IS FURTHER

ORDERED: That the collection of tax required by Code Section 48-8-30 upon the retail
purchase, retail sale, rental, storage, use, or consumption of fuel to a
contract or common carrier regulated by the United States Surface
Transportation Board for use exclusively in the operation of locomotives by
such carrier is hereby suspended for the effective dates of this Order.

IT IS FURTHER

ORDERED: That if one or more of the provisions contained in this Order shall be held
to be invalid, in violation of the Georgia Constitution, in violation of
Georgia law, or unenforceable in any respect, such invalidity, violation, or
unenforceability shall not affect any other provisions of this Order, but, in
such case, this Order shall be construed as if such invalid, illegal, or
unenforceable provision had never been contained within the Order.

IT IS FURTHER

ORDERED: That no provision of this Order shall limit, infringe, suspend, or supplant
any judicial order, judgment, or decree issued pursuant to the laws or
constitution of this State or the laws or constitution of the United States,
nor shall any person use any provision this Order as a defense to an action
in violation of a judicial order, judgment, or decree by any court created
pursuant to the laws or constitution of this State or the laws or constitution
of the United States.

IT IS FURTHER
ORDERED: The Office of the Governor may continue to issue guidance on the scope of

this Order as needed through communication media, including social
media, without need for further Executive Orders.

IT IS FURTHER
ORDERED: That the provisions of this Order shall be effective upon signature and shall

expire Monday, September 12, 2022, at 11:59 P.M., unless otherwise
renewed or terminated via subsequent Executive Order.

The State of Georgia is committed to helping small businesses expand and
create jobs; and

Small businesses are important to the growth and success of Georgia's
economy and are responsible for employing nearly half of Georgia’s
workforce; and

Georgia’s agencies are currently required to offer information about
procurement opportunities with the state; and

The process to enter into procurement contracts with the state can be
difficult for small businesses to navigate; and

The Department of Administrative Services (“DOAS”) provides various
opportunities for small businesses to learn and participate in the state
procurement process such as the Small Business Procurement Readiness
Workshop series, the Small Business Symposium series, and the Minority
Business Enterprise certification process; and

DOAS has the statutory duty to administer the state procurement process
pursuant to Code Section 50-5-51, et seq.

NOW, THEREFORE, PURSUANT TO THE AUTHORITY VESTED IN ME AS
GOVERNOR OF THE STATE OF GEORGIA, IT IS HEREBY

That DOAS shall create the position of Small Business and Supplier
Diversity Manager and create a position to facilitate communications and
engagement with minority-owned small businesses.

IT IS FURTHER
That DOAS shall schedule and hold regular meetings with representatives

from small business community stakeholders and small business
development partners, including chambers of commerce in order to help

ORDERED:

ORDERED:

ORDERED:

ORDERED:

ORDERED:

better understand the challenges faced by small businesses and identify
obstacles to participation in the state procurement process.

IT IS FURTHER

Through these meetings, DOAS shall increase active outreach efforts to the
small business community with a particular focus on the minority-owned,
women-owned, and veteran-owned business community - these efforts
shall include, but are not limited to, supplier education and training.

IT IS FURTHER

That DOAS shall coordinate with the Georgia Department of Economic
Development’s Director of Small Business Outreach and other small
business development partners, such as the University of Georgia’s Small
Business Development Center Multicultural Business Division, to hold
these regular meetings and increase active outreach efforts to the small
business community.

IT IS FURTHER

By October 31, 2022, DOAS shall issue a report which provides specific
recommendations to implement which will assist in making the state
procurement process more easily accessible to small businesses.

IT IS FURTHER

That if one or more of the provisions contained in this Order shall be held
to be invalid, in violation of the Georgia Constitution, in violation of
Georgia law, or unenforceable in any respect, such invalidity, violation, or
unenforceability shall not affect any other provisions of this Order, but, in
such case, this Order shall be construed as if such invalid, illegal, or
unenforceable provision had never been contained within the Order.

IT IS FURTHER

That this Order shall be effective upon signature.

By letter dated June 29, 2022, the Georgia Sheriffs’ Association has
requested the appointment of a committee under Code Section
15-16-26 to investigate Pulaski County Sheriff Danny Brannen; and

Per its request, the Georgia Sheriffs’ Association has been informed
that Sheriff Brannen is not performing all the duties required by his
office due to incapacity; and

The Executive Committee of the Georgia Sheriffs’ Association
believes an investigation is warranted after inquiring into Sheriff
Brannen’s capacity to perform the functions of his office; and

Pursuant to the Georgia Sheriffs’ Association Executive Committee’s
request, as authorized by Code Section 15-16-26(a), I have
determined that an investigation of Sheriff Brannen should be made
due to the alleged incapacity of Sheriff Brannen to perform the
functions of his office; and

Code Section 15-16-26(a) provides that two sheriffs who are
members of the Georgia Sheriffs’ Association shall be appointed to
conduct the investigation along with the Attorney General.

NOw, THEREFORE, PURSUANT TO CODE SECTION 15-16-26 AND
THE AUTHORITY VESTED IN ME AS THE GOVERNOR OF THE STATE OF
GEORGIA, IT IS HEREBY

That Attorney General Christopher Carr, Sheriff Ezell Brown of
Newton County, and Sheriff Clay Whittle of Columbia County are
hereby appointed as the committee to investigate the alleged
incapacity of Sheriff Brannen to perform the functions of the Pulaski
County Sheriff's Office.

IT IS FURTHER

ORDERED: That the committee shall make a report of its investigation to me
within thirty (30) days of the date of this Order.

BY THE GOVERNOR:

SUSPENDING FUEL TAXES DURING THE STATE OF EMERGENCY

WHEREAS:

WHEREAS:

WHEREAS:

WHEREAS:

WHEREAS:

WHEREAS:

WHEREAS:

WHEREAS:

WHEREAS:

FOR SUPPLY CHAIN DISRUPTIONS

On April 14, 2022, due to the ongoing severe disruptions to Georgia’s
supply chain, I issued Executive Order 04.14.22.01, declaring a State of
Emergency for Supply Chain Disruptions; and

On May 10, 2022, I renewed the State of Emergency for Supply Chain
Disruptions until June 14, 2022, by issuing Executive Order 05.10.22.01;
and

On May 26, 2022, I renewed the State of Emergency for Supply Chain
Disruptions until July 14, 2022, by issuing Executive Order 05.26.22.01;
and

On July 1, 2022, I renewed the State of Emergency for Supply Chain
Disruptions until August 13, 2022, by issuing Executive Order 07.01.22.01;
and

On May 26, 2022, I issued Executive Order 05.26.22.02 suspending the
collection of motor fuel and diesel fuel taxes required by Code Section 48-
9-3 through July 14, 2022; and

The supply chain disruptions affecting the cost of fuel have not been fully
alleviated since I issued Executive Order 05.26.22.01, and the high cost of
fuel continues to negatively impact Georgia’s residents and economy; and

The Governor is vested with the emergency powers cited herein as the Chief
Executive of this State; and

Code Section 38-3-28 provides that “[a]ll orders, rules, and regulations
promulgated by the Governor” have the force and effect of law; and

As Chief Executive, the Governor is tasked with protecting the citizens of
this State, including during a state of emergency; and

WHEREAS:

WHEREAS:

WHEREAS:

WHEREAS:

WHEREAS:

WHEREAS:

ORDERED:

ORDERED:

ORDERED:

Code Section 38-3-51(c)(1) vests the Governor with the power to enforce all
laws, rules, and regulations relating to emergency management and to
assume direct operational control of all civil forces and helpers in the state;
and

Code Section 38-3-51(c)(4) vests the Governor with the power to perform
and exercise such other functions, powers, and duties as may be deemed
necessary to promote and secure the safety and protection of the civilian
population; and

Code Section 38-3-51(d)(1) vests the Governor with the power to suspend
any regulatory statute prescribing the procedures for conduct of state
business, or the orders, rules, or regulations of any state agency if strict
compliance with any statute, order, rule, or regulation would in any way
prevent, hinder, or delay necessary action in coping with the emergency or
disaster; and

Code Section 45-12-22 vests the Governor with the power to suspend the
collection of taxes, or any part thereof, due the state until the next meeting
of the General Assembly but no longer; and

In the event the Governor has declared a state of emergency, Code Section
45-12-22 vests him with the power to suspend the collection of state motor
fuel taxes, subject to ratification by the General Assembly at its next
meeting; and

In consultation with state economic, transportation, and emergency
preparedness officials, I have determined that the following actions are
necessary and appropriate to protect the continued strength of Georgia’s
economy and provide for the health, safety, and welfare of Georgia’s
residents and visitors.

NOW, THEREFORE, PURSUANT TO CODE SECTION 38-3-51, AND THE
AUTHORITY VESTED IN ME AS GOVERNOR OF THE STATE OF GEORGIA,
IT IS HEREBY

That pursuant to Code Section 45-12-22, the collection of motor fuel and
diesel fuel taxes required by Code Section 48-9-3 is hereby suspended for
the effective dates of this Order.

IT IS FURTHER

That no distributor of motor fuel or diesel fuel shall be found in violation
of Code Section 48-9-17 for complying with the terms of this Order.

IT IS FURTHER

That the collection of tax required by Code Section 48-8-30 upon the retail
purchase, retail sale, rental, storage, use, or consumption of fuel to a
contract or common carrier regulated by the United States Surface
Transportation Board for use exclusively in the operation of locomotives by
such carrier is hereby suspended for the effective dates of this Order.

FOR SUPPLY CHAIN DISRUPTIONS

On April 14, 2022, due to the ongoing severe disruptions to Georgia’s
supply chain, I issued Executive Order 04.14.22.01, declaring a State
of Emergency for Supply Chain Disruptions; and

On May 10, 2022, I renewed the State of Emergency for Supply Chain
Disruptions until June 14, 2022, by issuing Executive Order
05.10.22.01; and

On May 26, 2022, I renewed the State of Emergency for Supply Chain
Disruptions until July 14, 2022, by issuing Executive Order
05.26.22.01; and

The State is experiencing such state of emergency due to the impacts
of severe supply chain disruptions on the economy and social and
economic wellbeing of its residents; and

On March 18, 2022, I signed House Bill 304 into law suspending the
collection of state motor fuel taxes from 5:00 P.M. March 18, 2022
through May 31, 2022 at 11:59 P.M.;

The supply chain disruptions affecting the cost of motor fuel have not
been fully alleviated since the signing of House Bill 304 and the high
cost of fuel continues to negatively impact Georgia’s residents and
economy; and

The Governor is vested with the emergency powers cited herein as
the Chief Executive of this State; and

Code Section 38-3-28 provides that “[a]ll orders, rules, and
regulations promulgated by the Governor” have the force and effect
of law; and

WHEREAS:

WHEREAS:

ORDERED:

ORDERED:

As Chief Executive, the Governor is tasked with protecting the
citizens of this State, including during a state of emergency; and

Code Section 38-3-51(c)(1) vests the Governor with the power to
enforce all laws, rules, and regulations relating to emergency
management and to assume direct operational control of all civil
forces and helpers in the state; and

Code Section 38-3-51(c)(4) vests the Governor with the power to
perform and exercise such other functions, powers, and duties as
may be deemed necessary to promote and secure the safety and
protection of the civilian population; and

Code Section 38-3-51(d)(1) vests the Governor with the power to
suspend any regulatory statute prescribing the procedures for
conduct of state business, or the orders, rules, or regulations of any
state agency if strict compliance with any statute, order, rule, or
regulation would in any way prevent, hinder, or delay necessary
action in coping with the emergency or disaster; and

In the event the Governor has declared a state of emergency, Code
Section 45-12-22 vests him with the power to suspend the collection
of state motor fuel taxes, subject to ratification by the General
Assembly at its next meeting; and

In consultation with state economic, transportation, and emergency
preparedness officials, I have determined that the following actions
are necessary and appropriate to protect the continued strength of
Georgia’s economy and provide for the health, safety, and welfare of
Georgia’s residents and visitors.

NOW, THEREFORE, PURSUANT TO CODE SECTION 38-3-51, AND
THE AUTHORITY VESTED IN ME AS GOVERNOR OF THE STATE OF
GEORGIA, IT IS HEREBY

That pursuant to Code Section 45-12-22, the collection of motor fuel
and diesel fuel taxes required by Code Section 48-9-3 is hereby
suspended for the effective dates of this Order.

IT IS FURTHER
That no distributor of motor fuel or diesel fuel shall be found in

violation of Code Section 48-9-17 for complying with the terms of this
Order.

restoration of Georgia’s social and economic welfare by responding

preparedness officials, I have determined the state of emergency
created by continued supply chain disruptions persists in the State of

The State of Georgia is experiencing significant challenges in the hiring and
retention of healthcare workers, including, but not limited to, nurses,
physicians, respiratory therapists, emergency medical personnel, and other
clinical and nonclinical personnel; and

These challenges were exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic; and

The shortage of healthcare workers has had a negative impact on Georgia’s
healthcare infrastructure and the ability of Georgia residents to access
healthcare services; and

To ensure the future health of Georgians and Georgia’s healthcare system,
it is imperative for state government and industry leaders to examine the
current state of our healthcare workforce and identify strategies and
recommendations for promoting increased workforce availability, hiring,
and retention.

NOW, THEREFORE, PURSUANT TO THE AUTHORITY VESTED IN ME AS
GOVERNOR OF THE STATE OF GEORGIA, IT IS HEREBY

That the Healthcare Workforce Commission is hereby established.
IT IS FURTHER

That the Healthcare Workforce Commission shall conduct a thorough study
of the state’s current healthcare workforce pipeline, including, but not
limited to, identifying significant data trends in healthcare workforce
changes and areas of concern within the existing pipeline, and shall make
recommendations for improvements to said pipeline, including, but not
limited to, recommendations regarding the expansion of education

strengthen the pipeline, scholarship and loan forgiveness programs that
may support workforce initiatives, investments in technology to improve

healthcare workforce.

IT IS FURTHER

That the Healthcare Workforce Commission shall make a report of its
findings and recommendations to the Governor no later than December 31,
2022.

been detrimentally impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic; and

the social and economic wellbeing of its residents; and

disruptions; and

the Chief Executive of this State; and

regulations promulgated by the Governor” have the force and effect
of law; and

As Chief Executive, the Governor is tasked with protecting the
citizens of this State, including during a state of emergency; and

Code Section 38-3-51(c)(1) vests the Governor with the power to
enforce all laws, rules, and regulations relating to emergency
management and to assume direct operational control of all civil
forces and helpers in the state; and

perform and exercise such other functions, powers, and duties as

Mr. Royce Reeves, Ward 2 Commissioner on the Cordele City

Officer, one count of Criminal Trespass, and one count of Disorderly
Conduct; and

The indictment was transmitted to the Governor pursuant to
O.C.G.A. § 45-5-6(b), and the certified copy was received on August
11, 2021; and

On September 7, 2021, I appointed Attorney General Christopher
Carr, Barnesville City Councilmember/Mayor Pro Tem Christopher
Hightower, and McDonough City Councilmember Benjamin Pruett
as the Review Commission to determine whether the indictment
related to and adversely affected the administration of the office of
Commissioner Reeves such that the rights and interests of the public
were adversely affected thereby, and to issue a written report within
fourteen days with a recommendation as to whether said
commissioner should be suspended from office as required by
O.C.G.A. § 45-5-6(e): and

On October 21, 2021, pursuant to a request from the Review
Commission, I extended the deadline for the Review Commission’s
report and recommendation to December 14, 2021; and

On January 20, 2022, the Review Commission issued its report
finding that the indictment of Royce Reeves does relate to and
adversely affect the administration of the office of Commissioner,
and that the rights and interests of the public are adversely affected
thereby; and recommending that Royce Reeves be suspended from
office pursuant to the provisions of O0.C.G.A. § 45-5-6; and

On January 21, 2022, pursuant to the recommendation of the Review
Commission, I issued Executive Order 01.21.22.01 suspending Mr.
Reeves from his office as Ward 2 Commissioner on the Cordele City
Commission; and

WHEREAS:

ORDERED:

Mr. Reeves, through counsel, on February 3, 2022, petitioned for a
review of his suspension as Ward 2 Cordele City Commissioner
under O.C.G.A. § 45-5-6(f).

NOw, THEREFORE, BY VIRTUE OF THE AUTHORITY VESTED IN ME AS
GOVERNOR OF THE STATE OF GEORGIA, IT IS HEREBY

That pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 45-5-6(f), Attorney General Christopher
Carr, Barnesville City Councilmember/Mayor Pro Tem Christopher
Hightower, and McDonough City Councilmember Benjamin Pruett
are hereby re-appointed as the Review Commission to review the
suspension of Mr. Royce Reeves as Ward 2 Cordele City
Commissioner and to make a written report within 14 days.

HEREBY

flown at half-staff on all state buildings and grounds on Saturday, February

STATE OF EMERGENCY FOR WINTER STORM

The National Weather Service issued a Winter Storm Watch for
Northeast Georgia, beginning on January 15, 2022; and

The Winter Storm Watch forecasts that areas of Georgia north of
Interstate 20 will likely be affected by potentially significant
accumulations of ice, snow, freezing rain, and sleet; and

This winter storm may result in accumulated snowfall totals ranging
from two to five (2-5) inches, with the potential for much larger
amounts in the higher elevations of Northeast Georgia; and

The Winter Storm Watch predicts one-quarter of an inch of ice in
affected areas which may continue to spread and impact more of the
State as the severe weather travels down to the Metro Atlanta area;
and

The wind gusts of 25 to 35 miles per hour projected to accompany
the storm will exacerbate any potential damage to public and private
property, including power outages and downed trees; and

Due to the possibility of black ice accumulating on roadways, the
winter storm poses a danger to the people of Georgia; and

Assistance from the State of Georgia is necessary to provide for the
public's health, safety, and welfare, protect public and private
property, and mitigate consequences of this winter storm; and

The Federal Motor Carrier Safety regulation, 49 C.F.R. 390, et seq.,
limit the hours of operators of commercial motor vehicles may drive;

IT IS FURTHER

That the Georgia Department of Transportation and Georgia
Department of Public Safety shall take all necessary action to ensure
the expeditious movement of utility vehicles, equipment, and
personnel through the State to eliminate power outages.

IT IS FURTHER

That all state agencies shall provide sufficient personnel required for
the staffing of the Georgia State Operations Center or other
command, control, and coordination points as may be designated by
the Director of the Georgia Emergency Management and Homeland
Security Agency and shall provide such personnel, vehicles,
equipment, and other resources needed to protect life and property
and to ensure continuation, restoration, and recovery of essential
public services.

IT IS FURTHER

That the federal rules and regulations limiting hours that operators
of commercial vehicles may drive are suspended to ensure the
uninterrupted supply of petroleum products; supplies; goods and
services. This declared emergency justifies a suspension of Part 395
(driver's hours of service) of Title 49 of the Code of Federal
Regulations. The suspension will remain in effect for thirty (30) days
or until the emergency condition ceases to exist, whichever is less.

of ten (10) feet, and an overall length of one hundred (100)

B. Ifthe width of said vehicle exceeds eight (8) feet six (6) inches

proper oversize signs, markings, flags, and escorts as defined
